items.question: What does it mean to be a shepherd over a small group of people?
items.book: What It Means to Become a Shepherd
items.text:
Being a shepherd over a small group means you see those people as sheep and relate with them as such — a caring, loving guide whom God has called to look after them [1][3]. Your work is specific: you have time to care, time to love, time to feed, and time to gather the sheep [1]. Jesus told Peter to prove his love by feeding and caring for the sheep — "Feed my lambs... Feed my sheep" (John 21:15-17) [3][4].

It is a great honour to be chosen from among men for this, to have a job in things pertaining to God, to relate to God directly on behalf of people, and to be chosen to have compassion on the ignorant [2]. You are privileged to help people prosper, to provide good food for the sheep, and to lead them — "He maketh me to lie down in green pastures... He leadeth me beside the still waters" (Psalm 23:2) [5]. And it matters for the sheep's safety: when the sheep are together in a group they are safer, and it is the shepherd who gathers them [8].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 1 and 2 of *What It Means to Become a Shepherd* and chapters 2 and 3 of *The Privilege*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 23:1-2; Psalms 95:6-7; Matthew 9:36; John 21:15-17.

items.question: How should I respond to people who try to turn me against my church leaders?
items.text:
Our books speak to this. Watch out for people who campaign against your fathers, trying to make you turn against your own father [2]. Those who do this are like Absalom, who stole the hearts of the men of Israel (2 Samuel 15:6, 15:13) [2]. And Jesus Himself said, "Tonight, you will be offended because of me" (Matthew 26:31), so do not be offended when a man of God you love is under fire, for it is normal for God's servants to go through fiery trials [6].

You should also know that those who love you will never believe bad things about you [6], and that the stories out there are often far from the truth [6].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 8 of *Those who are Dangerous Sons* and chapter 8 of *Those Who Are Offended*.

Scriptures referenced: 2 Samuel 15:6; 2 Samuel 15:13; Matthew 26:31.

items.question: What does the Bible say about people who rebel against their leaders in church?
items.text:
The books speak plainly about this. A rebel is someone who defies authority, openly opposes and challenges the leadership, refuses to obey rules, and does not behave as a subordinate ought to [2]. Rebellion is not a small matter: Scripture says "rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft" (1 Samuel 15:23), and it is counted a unique sin, distinct from every other [1][7]. God even told Israel through Joshua, "He will not forgive your rebellion and your sins" (Joshua 24:19) [7][8].

Such a person is described as an evil man who seeks only rebellion (Proverbs 17:11), stubborn and stiff-necked (Deuteronomy 31:27), and one who becomes a man of darkness and secrets, murmuring in secret while smiling to your face [5][7][8]. The counsel given is to mark and avoid them, as Romans 16:17 says, "mark them which cause divisions and offences… and avoid them" [6], and to abhor those in rebellion, as Psalm 139:21 says, so that you do not become a rebel yourself [3]. Rebels are also said to desire alternative leadership, appointing a captain to return to their bondage (Nehemiah 9:17) [3].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 4 of *How you can become a strong Christian*, chapters 1, 4 and 8 of *Those Who Rebel* and chapter 4 of *Loyalty and Disloyalty*.

Scriptures referenced: Deuteronomy 31:27; Joshua 1:17-18; Joshua 22:19; Joshua 24:19; 1 Samuel 15:23; Nehemiah 9:17; Job 34:37; Psalms 139:21; Proverbs 17:11; Ecclesiastes 1:9 and 3 more.

items.question: What difference does it make whether I serve the Lord or not?
items.book: It Is A Great Thing To Serve The Lord
items.text:
The books say there will always be a difference between those who serve the Lord and those who do not [1]. Malachi 3:17-18 promises that God will spare His servants as a man spares his own son, and then you will discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serves God and him that serves Him not [1][8].

The clearest picture is the two sons. The one who stayed and served was a joint heir, told by his father, "All that I have is thine" (Luke 15:31), while the one who left was lost and dead, and is alive and found only when he returns (Luke 15:32) [2][3]. Isaiah 65:12-14 also warns that God's servants shall eat, drink, rejoice and sing for joy of heart, while those who do not serve shall be hungry, thirsty, ashamed and cry for sorrow of heart [4]. And Deuteronomy 28:47-48 says that because you did not serve the Lord your God with joyfulness, you shall serve your enemies in hunger, thirst and want of all things [5][7].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 4, 8 and 10 of *It Is A Great Thing To Serve The Lord*.

Scriptures referenced: Deuteronomy 28:47-48; Psalms 65:4; Psalms 73:27-28; Isaiah 65:12-14; Malachi 3:17-18; Luke 15:15; Luke 15:17; Luke 15:21; Luke 15:29; Luke 15:31-32 and 1 more.

items.question: How does God give revelation to people today if it's not always through visions?
items.text:
Yes, our books speak to this. The spirit of revelation often manifests as visions and dreams, showing you what is happening behind the scenes, but it can also lead you to experiences that make you see, hear and know things few people ever experience [6]. John himself had two different manifestations: the fantastic visions on Patmos, and the "real life revelation" of being close to Jesus, seeing, looking upon and touching Him [1].

There is also revelation that comes without any vision at all. Jesus said, "Blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed" (John 20:29), and people who accomplish great things for God without seeing visions are even more blessed than those who have seen them [5]. For most of us, the path is meditation — thinking deeply about God's Word — since most of us will not have these special revelations and will have to depend on meditation [7]. And a great blessing can come simply by reading, for "Blessed is he that readeth" (Revelation 1:3) [5].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 2 of *Victory Secrets*, chapter 30 of *How To Neutralize Curses* and chapter 6 of *Rules of Full Time Ministry (2nd edition)*.

Scriptures referenced: John 20:29; Ephesians 1:15-18; 1 Timothy 4:16; 1 John 1:1; 1 John 1:3; Revelation 1:3.

items.question: How do I deal with people in the church who are disloyal or stealing from the offering?
items.text:
Friend, the books speak to both of these plainly.

On disloyal people: you are to direct firmness at quieting, humbling, warning and controlling them [1]. Deal with all disloyal separatists the way God dealt with Satan — throw them out, have no more meetings with them, don't discuss their ideas and visions with them [2]. Dismiss disloyal, disobedient or offending workers completely, even longstanding ones, though in mercy make financial provision so they can live and work elsewhere without hardship, so the root of bitterness does not spread, as Hebrews 12:15 warns [3]. This rests on Proverbs 22:10, "Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out" [5][6]. Questionable loyalty is diagnosed when someone makes malicious or poisonous comments, or keeps close ties with an openly disloyal person [5]. And note that absolute evidence is not needed — being a mysterious person is deemed enough evidence for dismissal [3].

On the offering: direct firmness at humbling, warning and controlling thieves in the church, for there are people stealing the offering you receive [1]. Prevent the loss by monitoring who becomes an usher, keeping ushers in view at all times, and ensuring security so no intruder can steal [7][8]. Have two or three count the money at the same time, never leave anyone alone with it, use a signed form matching the bank pay-in slips, keep it in a secure safe, and bank 100% of it promptly [7][8]. Offerings should not be kept in the pastor's house, lest he be accused of misusing the church's money [7][8].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 6 of *A Good General*, chapter 12 of *One of You is a Devil*, chapter 77 of *The Gift Of Governments*, chapter 8 of *Pillars of Loyalty*, chapter 10 of *Church Growth* and chapter 3 of *Church Administration*.

Scriptures referenced: 2 Samuel 15:11; Proverbs 22:10; Titus 1:5; Hebrews 12:15.

items.question: What happens to a person who dies without being born again?
items.text:
Friend, the books speak plainly to this. When you die you will either go to Heaven or Hell — you will not just stop existing, but head for a permanent destination away from this earth [4]. The rich man in Luke 16:22-23 died and in hell lifted up his eyes, being in torments, while Lazarus was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom [4].

And this is not a rare or difficult fate to reach: because sin came into the world through one man and death spread to all men, every unsaved soul is bound to end up in hell, from the President to the poorest man in the village [2]. Even if we just sit down doing nothing, minding our own business, we will still end up there [2]. Unless a man is born again spiritually and reconciled to God through Christ, he is headed for Hell [2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 11 of *People Who Went to Hell* and chapter 4 of *How to be Born again & Avoid Hell*.

Scriptures referenced: Luke 16:19-31; Romans 5:12.

judged.sentence: When you die you will either go to Heaven or Hell — you will not just stop existing, but head for a permanent destination away from this earth.
The rich man in Luke 16:22-23 died and in hell lifted up his eyes, being in torments, while Lazarus was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom.

And this is not a rare or difficult fate to reach: because sin came into the world through one man and death spread to all men, every unsaved soul is bound to end up in hell, from the President to the poorest man in the village.
Even if we just sit down doing nothing, minding our own business, we will still end up there.
Unless a man is born again spiritually and reconciled to God through Christ, he is headed for Hell.
